headers.//: index.html must never be served from cache. Firebase Hosting defaults to max-age=3600, and index.html is the file that names the current content-hashed bundle (entry-<hash>.js). Every export produces a new hash and the previous bundle is removed on deploy, so a browser holding an hour-old index.html requested a JS file that no longer existed and rendered nothing at all - which is why the app intermittently failed to load until cookies and cache were cleared by hand.
Same for the bare route and any client-side route resolved through the SPA rewrite above - all of them return index.html.
The opposite treatment for the hashed assets: their filenames change whenever their contents do, so they can be cached indefinitely and a returning visitor re-downloads nothing.
